assessment: Both banks completed all 384 sweeps and passed structural, numerical, independence, and exact replay checks. The severe Stage-5B selection separation did not persist: selection full-window median/max KS were 0.09180/0.13672 (half-window maxima 0.25000 and 0.30469), and calibration median/max were 0.09180/0.16797 (half-window maxima 0.31250 and 0.18750). Every retained state was unique within its walker. Cross-bank pooled KS was 0.10498 overall (0.09375 and 0.13867 by half), with comparable six-coordinate geometry: within-bank medians 0.25696 and 0.25911, cross-bank 0.26016. Calibration mean logL increased by about 249.25 between retained halves, versus 18.88 for selection; the second-half cross-bank mean gap was about 283.94. This residual drift is recorded, but the broad distributions overlap and neither bank shows severe persistent cross-walker separation. The finite-run evidence supports qualitatively compatible, usable populations under the stated validation criterion, without establishing full physical convergence.
consequence: Freeze pooled-with-replacement promotion and the population kernel; manual DNS methodology development is complete.

freeze.promotion_rule: Within each bank independently, uniformly sample eight saved strict eligible retained states with replacement; no donor optimization; duplicates permitted.
